Not just for Nadiamsa, accuracy of Ayanamsa is a must even in other cases, like Navamsa
Sapthamsa and Shashtiamsa. To wit, if a planet, say Saturn is in Aries 19deg 59’ as per Lahiri ayanamsa
another ayanamsa even with a small difference of minus 2’ of arc can place Saturn somewhat ahead
and give it Libra Navamsa instead of Virgo navamsa due to Lahiri. Saturn even in Aries Rasi with
Libra Navamsa protects one from heart ailments, gives him longevity and helps him progress in his
calling. The same Saturn with Aries sign position but in Virgo Nayasma makes him wholly unreliable
and makes him a victim of some sort of diseases of hand and legs. This difference could be easily located
by an experienced astrologer. Same is the case with other divisions including Nadiamsa.

1430-14301/2. Kahala Yoga: One born in
Kahala Yoga will be a minister or an army chief.
He will own more than ten thousand gold coins.
He will speak like a lord (i.e. superior in speech).
His 38th year will give him paternal riches.
Notes: It is not understandable whether
Kahala Yoga is discussed as a general principle or
with reference to Champaka Nadiamsa in Cancer
alone.
Kahala Yoga is formed when the 4th lord
and Jupiter are in mutual angles. Alternatively,
the 4th lord should be in his own sign or in exaltation. He must as well join the lord of the 10th.
For Cancer ascendant, Venus is the lord of
the 4th. He should be in an angle to Mars. Or
Venus should be in Libra/Taurus/Pisces in association with Mars. According to the text,
Kahala Yoga gives wealth exceeding "10,000 gold
coins" while the native’s 38th year will bestow on
him paternal wealth as well.
With Kahala Yoga in general according to
Parasara, the native will be endowed with a complete army of chariots, elephants, horses and infantry. He will lord over villages, be energetic and
adventurous.
As per C.G. Rajan, the 3rd kind of Kahala
Yoga is torn thus : The lords of fourth and 9th
should be in mutual angles while the ascendant
lord is endowed with strength.
Foolishness is also a part of Kahala Yoga.
Mantreswara gives a fourth kind of Kahala
Yoga in his Phala Deepika. The dispositor of the
dispositor of ascendant lord should be in exaltation, or own sign, identical with a trine/angle
counted from the ascendant.

Preface
I have great pleasure in presenting herewith Book II of Deva Keralam.
The encouragement given by the readers following appearance of Book I hereof is
thankfully acknowledged.
Although the original is popularly attributed to Achyuta, in actuality Venkatesa’s
name also appears as author at one stage. This Venkatesa need not be confused with
Sarvartha Chintamani’s author, vide notes given under sloka 1 infra. The original
authorship is actually divided as under:
Sloka No. 1 to 3407 by Achyuta in the first phase.
Sloka No. 1 to 4775 by Venkatesa in the later phase.
Thus there 1s a total of 8102 original slokas for which our arrangement of presentation
iS as under:
Sloka 1 to sloka 2718 of Achyuta in Book I.
Sloka 2719 to sloka 3407 of Achyuta, and sloka 1 to sloka 1997 of Venkatesa in Book
Rest of the work from slokas from No. 1998 to 4775 of Venkatesa is being brought
out as Book III.
In the present volumealso, there are many general principles applicable to the various
ascendants, apart from Nadiamsa discussions confined to given signs. The reader will be
able to understand the same as he progresses with the study of the text, remembering at the
same time the general outlines given in the preface for Book I.

cause great fear, danger in general and danger to life.

When Satur is in transit in the 2nd/4th stars, the king
of the country will die and the native will undergo

(d) If the birth star or the tenth therefrom is
occupied by a malefic at birth, Saturn’s transit in this
segment will create quarrels with king and consequent distress. In the absence of these effects,
physical illness to self, and nuisance from his own
men will come to pass. When a benefic transits in the
first or tenth Nakshatra, auspicious effects will occur
and malefics according to their natural disposition

third or eighth from it, evil transits of Jupiter and the

(g) Ifnatural benefics occupy one of these three

Notes: In the first instance, week days are divided
between benefic and malefic planets, thus: Monday,
Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are benefic days
ruled in order by the Moon (:rrespective of Paksha or
lunar half), Mercury (irrespective of his association),
Jupiter and Venus. Malefic week days are Sunday,
Tuesday and Saturday and are ruled by the Sun, Mars
and Saturn in that order. Now see the following
clarificatory notes.
Benefic week days will give wealth and happiness
in combination with other horoscopic influences.
“Birth star coinciding with week day ruled by........”
is an unintelligible clause.
When the day of birth is ruled by a malefic it will
make one prone to illness depending on the other
yogas in the horoscope.
The following classical quotations may be of interest.
One born on Sunday will be endangered in either
the first month or the 6th month, or in the 22nd/23rd
year. His life span will be 60 years.
Monday-born will face danger in the 11th month or
in the 26th/27th year. His life span will be 84 years.
Tuesday-born will be in trouble in the 2nd or 22n
year. He will be always sick and will live upto 74
years.
Wednesday-born willincur danger in the 8th month
or in the 8th year. He will die after his 64th year.
Thursday-born will be in danger in 7th month,
16th/13th year. He will live upto 84th year.
Friday-born will never fall sick. He will die in the
60th year.
Saturday-born will incurdangerin the 1st monthor
in the 13th year. His life will end in 100th year.

Notes: “Occupation” ofa malefic is not in our text,

translation.
“Aroodha Bhaga” is ascending degree, that is the
sign ascending at birth.
Planetary war: When two planets (except the
luminaries) are on the same degree there is sa si to be
a war between them. The one in the north is declared
victorious.
Amore clear picture is givenby C.G. Rajan. When
two planets out of the five, viz. Mars to Satu, are in
one and the same sign with longitudes of identical
degree, minute and second, a planetary war occurs.
The victor will have higher latitude.
I give below an example.
On 23rd August 23, 1992, Venus and Jupiterin Leo
attained the same degree, minute and second while
the latitude of Venus was 1° 17' North, and that of
Jupiter 1° 4. Hence Venus, with a higher latitude
Should be treated as winner.
Another planet that could be connected with the
ascendant by aspect of association is one inimical to
the lord of the ascendant. Example: Capricorn ascendant related to the Sun, dead enemy of ascendant
lord Saturn.
In each of these cases, the result is involvement in
quarrels, in the dasa periods of the concemed planet.
In case of the example of Capricorn, the dasa of the
Sun will give the said result.
Protection from the said adversity is a helpful
association of the ascendant with a benefic.

3035 - 3037. Dasa Effects: During the first Dasa
the native will have eating comforts, will beget
auspicious effects and various kinds of wealth apart
from grief. The second dasa will cause wealth,
happiness and apparels. Destruction of quadrupeds,
landed properties and money, and grief to one’s near
and dear will be produced by the third dasa. Additionally sickness, enmity with relatives, quarrels and
sudden outbursts of anger will follow. Inthe 4th dasa,
effects to occurare well-being, happiness, wealthand
worship. The fifth dasa will cause grief due to loss of
wealth following royal wrath. One will acquire inthe
sixth dasa happiness, wealth, success, lands, garlands
and robes. The seventh dasa will produce many a
kind of grief, difficulties and ailments due to vitiation
of three bodily temperaments viz. bile, wind and
phlegm. Acquisition of royal honours, ornaments,
conveyances, involvement in divine undertakings
and bed comforts will take place in the eighth dasa.
The last of all, the ninth dasa will cause friendliness
with the king and virtuous men, fondness for learning, obeying royal orders, arrival of sons, frends and
relatives and skill. These apart, one will be worried
on account of unwed progeny, will incur fever,
phlegmatic fevers and troubles to sitand to sleep, and
wander aimlessly, (The word “Subham” is a corrupt
addition at the end of the sloka No. 3037.)

Notes: For the part from sloka 1 above till the

do not know whether it is the same author with a

In the present context, the Gotra of the author is
given as Kasyapa and hence he was a descendant of
sage Kasyapa.
[Kasyapa was a mythical sage, husband of Aditi
and twelve other daughters of Daksha. By Aditi, he
was father of Adityas and of Maha Vishnu. By his
other twelve wives, he was father of demons, Nagas,
reptiles, birds and all kinds of living things. He was
one ofthe seven Great Rishis (Sapta Rishis) and priest
of Parasu Rama and Lord Sri Rama Chandra.]
The author Venkatesa was apparently enthused
bysome royal patronage to compile the present work.
He should not be confuséd with Sarvartha
Chintamani's author, Venkatesa Daivagna, who in
fact belonged to Bharadwaja Gotra.

Preface
Presented herewith is Book III of Deva Keralam (Chandra Kala Nadi) from sloka No. 1998 to
5774 (i.e. 3796 slokas) - the portion compiled by Venkatesa.
The arrangement of the book goes thus:
Sloka No. 1 to 2718 by Achyuta in Book I.
Sloka No. 2719 to 3407 of Achyuta, and sloka No.1 to 1997 of Venkatesa in Book II.
Sloka No. 1998 to 5774 by Venkatesa in Book III.
These 3 volumes put together have a total of 9181 slokas in all (3407 by Achyuta and 5774 by
Venkatesa) for which complete English translation has been provided by me.
As the discerning reader understands, the work covers two areas of delineation. A particular
space of rising degree called Nadiamsa is used to depict a series of events to occur in the native’s life,
one of the subtle techniques of handling a horoscope. On the other hand, countless general principles
are enumerated on the lines done by popular series of text-books like Parasara Hora, Phala Deepika,
Saravali, Jataka Parijata and Sarvartha Chintamani dealing with natal horoscopy including dasa
effects, transits and the like. In some cases, general principles that do not consider Nadiamsa
technique are incorporated in the Nadiamsa reading. To avoid confusion to the reader, these have
been separated by me in the translation, as far as possible. Further, these have been more clearly
sorted out in the index given at the end of the present volume. The index now given embraces all the
3 parts. |
As the reader knows, each sign has 150 Nadiamsas and the 12 signs have a total of 1800
Nadiamsas. It is not humanly possible to bring out a work dealing with all the 1800 Nadiamsas. To
the extent possible, the authors Achyuta and Venkatesa, gathered a large amount of information on
this most subtle division. An intelligent reader can multiply the use of a Nadiamsa four-fold keeping
in mind the three classifications of the 12 zodiacal signs into movable, fixed and common signs.
For example, a rule given for a certain Nadiamsa for Aries can be suitably extended to the other
three movable signs, viz. Cancer, Libra and Capricorn. Similarly the four fixed signs Taurus, Leo,
Scorpio and Aquarius can be brought under the second category. The three dual signs Gemini, Virgo,
Sagittarius and Pisces form part of the 3rd group. While doing so, the involvement of planets should
be judiciously understood. This is because the same planet plays a different role for each sign
ascending.
The text excels in merits in tactfully combining the usage of Vimsottari dasa and Kala Chakra
dasa. So also in applying transits with reference to the signs caused by certain Navamsa positions.
Many such rare techniques are available in this wonderful work. One who uses such techniques
frequently will be able to issue successful predictions.
I sincerely believe that the reader will find our present efforts useful and forgive me for my
shortcomings if any.
Mr. Narinder Sagar of Sagar Publications deserves special thanks for undertaking the task of
bringing out this voluminous work considering the huge amount of money that the production of a
book of this size requires.

Notes: This portion attempts to instruct us on

Moon. These and the 36 Chandra Velas are welldiscussed coherently in texts like Phala Deepika
and by Pandit late M. R. K. Bhat in his work,

and Chandra Avasthas are put forth by me as under
so that my job is completed in a satisfactory

Chandra Kriya (Moon's actions): One Nakshatra is 13° 20' or 800' of arc. Divide 800 by 60
and find out in what part of such a portion is the
Moon placed. That will be Chandra Kriya.
Example: Say the Moon is 2° 40’ of Aswini, i.e.
160th minute of longitude in Aswini. 160 divided
by 60 yields the 3rd Chandra Kriya. The result
mentioned for the 3rd Kriya will apply to the
Moon's particular position.
Also see slokas 2570 - 2578 infra for effects of
Chandra Kriyas. Our text gives another methd of
Chandra Kriya which are five per sign, and 60 in all
for 12 signs, which are found from sloka 2579
onward. |
Chandra Avasthas (Moon's states): There
are 12 specific Avasthas for the Moon which
should be found out by dividing 800 by 12. In
which of the 12th part is the Moon located in that
particular Nakshatra should thus be known which
will tell of Chandra Avastha. |
(Similarly for Chandra Vela, the divisor is 36
as there are 36 Chandra Velas, or the Moon's
periods.)
These can be used in respect of birth horoscope,
query horoscopes, Muhurta etc.

5750 - 5753. Rasi Divisions: (a) Thirty degrees
constitute a Rasi (lit. ascendant).
(b) Half of it is called Hora.
(c) Drekkana is a third of the sign.
(d) Dvadasamsa is one twelfth of a sign.
(e) Trimsamsa is constituted by thirtieth parts.
(f) The drekkana distribution should in order be
done thus: (to) the lords of the Ist, 5th and 9th in
case of movable signs, the lords of the 9th, Ist and
5th in case of immovable signs, and the 5th, 9th and
the Ist (in case of dual signs).
(g) For positions in Aries, Leo and Sagittarius
count from Aries. For Capricorn, Taurus and Virgo
count from Capricorn. For Libra, Aquarius and
Gemini, count from Libra. For Cancer, Scorpio
and Pisces, count from Cancer. (Thus are the
Navamsa distribution to be understood.)
